description: Machine-readable form of criteria.md: every scored criterion (C01-C43) with its group, tag, priority, suggested weight, what it asks, what the score is based on, and the allowed score values with suggested points. criteria.md stays the prose source; when a criterion changes there, change it here in the same commit. Rendered to docs/evaluation-matrix.pdf by docs/evaluation-matrix.typ.
status_of_weights_and_points: SUGGESTED, not yet adopted by Daniel (proposed by Agent (Claude Opus 5.5), 2026-10-31). Scorecards do not use them yet.

scoring.weights_basis: Derived from the priority tags in criteria.md: priority: top = 3, priority: high = 2, untagged = 1.
scoring.formula: tool_score = sum(weight_i * points_i) / sum(weight_i), over criteria whose value is not in excluded_values. Report the coverage (scored criteria / total) next to the score, since '?' cells are left out rather than scored 0.
scoring.group_score: Same formula restricted to one group, so groups can be compared without one dominating.
scoring.qualifier_note: Some criteria carry a qualifier as well as a score (e.g. C22 storage, C34 format, C13-C15 type). Qualifiers are recorded but not scored.

groups.name: Connector ecosystem
groups.summary: What connectors exist, who gets them, and whether integration is the product's core.

groups.name: Google Workspace
groups.summary: Native or catalogue Google access; custom-MCP-only scores Partial. Note personal vs Workspace accounts.

groups.name: Multiple accounts per connector
groups.summary: One connector type connected to several accounts (personal + work) in the same assistant.

groups.name: Connector usage and control
groups.summary: How connectors are invoked and what stops them acting without you.

groups.name: Own infrastructure and local tools
groups.summary: Reaching things you host: gateways, home network tools, your own servers.

groups.name: Data ownership
groups.summary: Getting your data out and keeping memory under your control.

groups.name: Agents, projects and coding
groups.summary: Work that outlives a single chat: background agents, project boundaries, the companion coding product.

groups.name: Clients and platforms
groups.summary: Official clients only; PWAs count only for C13 and must be labelled.

criteria.name: Purpose-built for integrations
criteria.asks: Is connecting an AI to external tools the platform's main purpose, or is it a general conversational tool with an integration feature added on?
criteria.basis: Judgement call from positioning, where connectors sit in the UI and docs, whether the product is usable at all without them, and depth of connector management (profiles, permissions, logs, testing).

criteria.name: Connector catalogue size
criteria.asks: How many ready-to-integrate connectors can a user switch on without writing or hosting anything?
criteria.basis: Approximate count with date and place counted (directory page, docs, in-app); who builds them (vendor, partner, community); whether bring-your-own connectors are also allowed (note only).

criteria.name: Official connector directory: URLs
criteria.asks: Is the connector library published at an official URL a human can browse, and as a programmatic list (JSON or API/registry endpoint) an agent can read?
criteria.basis: Both URLs; whether the JSON needs auth; fields carried (name, description, auth type, MCP URL); official vs community mirror (mirrors do not count).

criteria.name: Custom MCP connections
criteria.asks: Can the user add their own MCP server, not just pick from the catalogue?
criteria.basis: Remote (URL) and/or local (stdio); transports (streamable HTTP, SSE); auth (OAuth, bearer/API-key header, none); tiers; clients (web, desktop, mobile); admin approval on business plans; tool limits per server.

values.meaning: mode-gated, admin-only, read-only tools or desktop-only

criteria.name: Native private connectors
criteria.asks: Is there native support for private connectors you or your org build and use without publishing them publicly?
criteria.basis: Mechanism (custom MCP URL, unlisted/draft app, org-private catalogue, developer mode); who can create and see it; tiers; auth options; whether vendor review is needed.

values.meaning: first-class private connectors shared with chosen people
only a per-user custom MCP URL, or business plans only

criteria.name: Plugin authorship and listing
criteria.asks: How does a third party get a connector listed in the official directory?
criteria.basis: Submission URL; requirements (MCP server, manifest, privacy policy, security review, verified domain); review time; fees or revenue share; whether individuals can publish.

criteria.name: Progressive tool discovery and tool limits
criteria.asks: Are tool definitions loaded up front, or discovered progressively (tool search, deferred loading)? What limits apply to the number of tools?
criteria.basis: Documented and observed limits (per server, per chat, total servers); behaviour at the limit (error, truncation, dropped tools); whether progressive loading covers custom MCP servers.

criteria.name: Plugin packaging format
criteria.asks: How is a plugin (bundle of connectors, instructions, skills, commands) packaged and declared? Open standard or proprietary?
criteria.basis: Manifest file and schema with spec link; what a plugin can contain; install from local path or Git URL; whether the package works in another vendor's tool.

criteria.name: Custom marketplaces
criteria.asks: Can you add your own plugin marketplaces beyond the vendor's? How many, and in what format?
criteria.basis: How a marketplace is declared (Git repo with manifest, JSON URL, MCP registry API); limit on marketplaces; whether private (authenticated) marketplaces work; sync across clients.

values.meaning: record the number allowed or Unlimited
admin-only, or one private catalogue on business plans

criteria.name: Connector access by subscription tier
criteria.asks: Is connector access restricted by tier, available to every paying subscriber, or free?
criteria.basis: Which tiers get what; cheapest tier with connector access and its monthly price (currency and region; no US egress); whether custom connectors are gated differently from catalogue ones.

criteria.name: Subscription pricing and restrictions
criteria.asks: What does each tier cost, and what restrictions affect agentic use (message/credit caps, connector or account caps, task limits, seat minimums, annual-only billing)?
criteria.basis: Every tier with price, currency and period as displayed (region noted); what each tier unlocks for connectors; documented restrictions; pricing page link and date read.

score.record: cheapest tier that gets C03-C12 at their best level for that tool, e.g. 'Plus $20/mo'
score.note: Price bands are a suggestion; convert to one currency at the date read before banding.

criteria.name: Google Workspace integration
criteria.asks: Does the platform support Google Workspace integration at all?
criteria.basis: How access is provided: native vendor connector or third-party catalogue connector (count as Yes) vs custom MCP only (Partial); personal accounts, Workspace accounts, or both.

criteria.name: Google Drive access level
criteria.asks: Is Google Drive access read-only or read-write?
criteria.basis: File types searched/read (Docs, Sheets, arbitrary files); whether write means creating new files, editing existing ones, or both; connector route as for C03.

criteria.name: Gmail access level
criteria.asks: Is Gmail access read-only or read-write?
criteria.basis: Whether write means sending directly, drafts only (scored Read-write, noted), or labelling/archiving; connector route as for C03.

criteria.name: Gmail attachments
criteria.asks: Does the Gmail integration support attachments?
criteria.basis: Whether incoming attachments can be read and whether mail can be sent or drafted with attachments.

criteria.name: Google Contacts access level
criteria.asks: Is Google Contacts access read-only or read-write?
criteria.basis: Whether contacts can be created and edited, or only searched and read; connector route as for C03.

criteria.name: Google Calendar access level
criteria.asks: Is Google Calendar access read-only or read-write?
criteria.basis: Whether write means creating, editing/deleting events, or both; whether non-primary calendars are visible; connector route as for C03.

criteria.name: Multiple accounts per connector
criteria.asks: Can the same connector be connected more than once, to different accounts (profiles)?
criteria.basis: Observed or documented ability to add a second instance of one connector (reference: ChatGPT, two Gmail connectors, observed by Daniel 2026-10-31).

values.meaning: only via a duplicate custom MCP server, or one active at a time

criteria.name: Profile naming / aliases
criteria.asks: Can each connected profile be given its own name or alias (e.g. 'Gmail personal', 'Gmail work')?
criteria.basis: Whether aliasing exists, and whether the alias is visible to the model or only in the settings UI.

criteria.name: Profile limit per connector
criteria.asks: Is there a maximum number of profiles per connector, or per account?
criteria.basis: The limit and whether it is documented or observed.

score.note: Bands are a suggestion; criteria.md records the raw number.

criteria.name: Profile selection handling
criteria.asks: When several profiles of one connector exist, how do you specify which one to use?
criteria.basis: Mechanisms available (naming in the prompt, per-chat toggle, per-project default, composer picker, automatic); behaviour when ambiguous (asks, guesses, uses all).

criteria.name: Connector invocation mode
criteria.asks: Are connectors available in ordinary chat, or only in a specific mode, model or project setting?
criteria.basis: Exact mode/toggle names; whether custom and catalogue connectors behave differently; whether it differs between web, desktop and mobile; what a gating mode loses.

criteria.name: Human-in-the-loop controls
criteria.asks: Is there deterministic, user-configurable control over when the assistant must ask before a connector action runs?
criteria.basis: Where settings live; 'remember for this chat' vs 'always'; whether policy covers custom connectors; how approval works for background tasks (prompt, push, task waits vs fails).

criteria.name: Autonomy modes and permission structure
criteria.asks: What levels of agent supervision exist, from fully supervised to fully autonomous, and how is the permission structure built?
criteria.basis: Mode names; how rules are expressed (per tool, command pattern, path, connector); where stored (user, project, admin policy) and which layer wins; mid-session switching; whether chat app and CLI share the model.

criteria.name: Team federation of plugin access
criteria.asks: On team plans, can an admin add connectors once for the org, allow/block them, scope them to groups, and choose per-user vs shared credentials?
criteria.basis: Admin location; SSO/SCIM group-driven access; per-user vs service credentials; pushing custom/private connectors to members; audit logging; tier needed.

criteria.name: Distributed deployments / satellites
criteria.asks: Is there built-in support for a network of deployments, e.g. the main app delegating to a CLI on a local server acting as a satellite?
criteria.basis: How instances are paired and authenticated; whether the satellite uses its local tools/files for the main app; whether it works from mobile.

values.meaning: remote control of one CLI session, no delegation
only by wrapping the CLI as an MCP server

criteria.name: Tunnels to own infrastructure / AI gateway
criteria.asks: Can the assistant reach your own infrastructure (home server, private network, own MCP/AI gateway)? How?
criteria.basis: Implementation; auth supported in front of the tunnel (e.g. Cloudflare Access service-token headers vs OAuth only); user feedback from forums, GitHub issues, Reddit with links and dates.

criteria.name: Locally hosted tool integration (e.g. Home Assistant)
criteria.asks: How would the platform reach and control a locally hosted tool like Home Assistant natively?
criteria.basis: The concrete Home Assistant route (official connector, HA MCP server integration, desktop app on the LAN); which clients it works from; user reports.

criteria.name: Output routing to own storage
criteria.asks: Can conversations, outputs or files be routed as they happen to storage you own (Drive folder, S3/R2, Git repo, webhook, local folder)?
criteria.basis: Destinations supported; automatic vs manual; format (Markdown, JSON). Expected to be rare (not seen anywhere by Daniel, 2026-10-31).

criteria.name: Backup / export API
criteria.asks: Is there a native API or scheduled export for getting your data out (conversations, projects, memory, files)?
criteria.basis: What is included (memory and project files often missing); format; whether business plans get a compliance/export API consumer plans don't.

criteria.name: Bring your own memory
criteria.asks: Is there first-party support for using your own memory store, or are you forced onto the built-in memory?
criteria.basis: Whether built-in memory can be disabled, viewed, edited and exported; whether an external memory connector is an official backend or a workaround.

criteria.name: Agent-to-agent (A2A) support
criteria.asks: Can the assistant call, be called by, and delegate between agents? Via an open protocol (e.g. A2A) or a proprietary one?
criteria.basis: Direction (calls, is called, both); protocol and version; auth between agents; whether delegated agents keep their tools and connectors; how results return. Links to C31.

criteria.name: Background agents, scheduled tasks and reminders
criteria.asks: Can you create background or persistent agents that run without an open chat, and schedule future tasks and reminders?
criteria.basis: Where they run (vendor cloud, your machine); connector and custom MCP access; delivery (push, email, in chat); limits on number/frequency; whether they run with all clients closed. Links to C20.

values.meaning: reminders only, or tasks without connector access

criteria.name: Project boundaries and where project data lives
criteria.asks: Can you define projects that bound context, files, instructions and connectors? Is project data in the cloud or local?
criteria.basis: What a project scopes (instructions, files, memory, history, connectors); whether memory leaks across projects or can be isolated; cross-device sync.

criteria.name: Parallel CLI coding product
criteria.asks: Does the vendor ship a CLI coding agent alongside the chat assistant, and how does it relate to the chat app?
criteria.basis: Product name; same subscription or not; whether chat-app connectors/MCP carry over to the CLI; whether a cloud coding agent shows up in the chat app.

score.note: criteria.md scores Yes/No plus a relationship; the relationship values above imply Yes.

criteria.name: CLI working-directory binding
criteria.asks: How tightly is the CLI bound to the directory it was launched in?
criteria.basis: Enforcement by permission system or sandbox; how extra directories are added (flag, command, config); whether config and memory are keyed to the CWD; whether it can run from ~ as a general assistant.

criteria.name: Native GitHub integration
criteria.asks: Is there a native, vendor-supported GitHub integration, rather than only a custom MCP server or the CLI calling gh?
criteria.basis: Connector vs GitHub App vs OAuth; private repo and org access; supported actions; chat, coding agent, or both; whether the cloud coding agent can open PRs.

criteria.name: Linux desktop app
criteria.asks: Is there an official Linux desktop app?
criteria.basis: Distribution channels (deb, rpm, AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, AUR, tarball); for a PWA, how it installs and what it loses (global hotkey, local MCP, dictation). Community clients score No and are named.

criteria.name: Linux CLI
criteria.asks: Is there an official CLI client that runs on Linux and uses the same account/subscription (not just a raw API key)?
criteria.basis: Install type (npm, pip/uv, binary, Homebrew, apt/repo, cargo, go install, Docker); whether it works only with API billing.

criteria.name: Android app
criteria.asks: Is there an official Android app?
criteria.basis: Distribution channel (Play Store, APK, F-Droid; PWA scores No unless it is the vendor's official Android app).

criteria.name: Cross-device conversation history sync
criteria.asks: Is conversation history synced through the cloud across web, desktop, Android and CLI?
criteria.basis: Which clients are in the sync and which keep history local.

criteria.name: Native speech-to-text, desktop
criteria.asks: Does the desktop client (or web app, if no desktop app) have built-in voice dictation into the chat input?
criteria.basis: Dictation vs full voice-conversation mode; whether it works on the Linux client specifically.

criteria.name: Native speech-to-text, Android
criteria.asks: Does the Android app have built-in voice dictation beyond the system keyboard's?
criteria.basis: Dictation vs voice mode; language support (Hebrew if known).
